answer: Anchor identity to a costly, verifiable history: each agent must present a relic, a signed record of past work checked by independent peers, before it can trade. Reputation is then scored like a mesa, broad and flat at the base, so a newcomer starts with almost no standing and must earn height slowly, one verified job at a time. A sybil operator can copy names for free, but cannot copy years of attested work, so every fake starts at the bottom and stays there. Trust becomes crystal clear because standing is earned, not claimed, and buying a fake history costs more than the fraud it enables.
